title: Third-Party Data Processing Annex (Partner Integrations) - Template v0.9 (Draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This Data Processing Annex ("Annex") is intended to be attached to and incorporated into a Master Services Agreement ("MSA") or Partner Agreement between the parties (Controller and Processor). It provides Annex-level detail for scenarios where Processor (including its third-party partner connectors, on-premise deployments, or hybrid deployments) processes personal data on behalf of Controller for partner integrations, connector deployments, or joint-customer projects.

Key drafting notes (internal):
- This template is partner-facing but prefers Controller-friendly protections for: subprocessor transparency, breach notification timing, audit rights, and cross-border transfer safeguards.
- Include negotiation options for enterprise customers that require on-site/air-gapped deployments.
- Add a short annex to cover embeddings and derived vector data (treatment as personal data if re-identifiable).

1. Definitions
For purposes of this Annex, capitalized terms shall have the meanings set out in the MSA. In addition: 
- "Personal Data": any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person processed under the Agreement.
- "Partner Connector": a Processor-hosted or third-party-hosted integration that transmits Controller data to or from third-party systems.
- "Subprocessor": any natural or legal person who processes Personal Data on behalf of Processor.

2. Roles and responsibilities
- Controller: determines purposes and means of processing.
- Processor: processes Personal Data on behalf of Controller in accordance with the Agreement and this Annex. Processor will maintain written records of processing activities related to Controller data.

3. Processing details (attach Appendix A where applicable)
- Subject-matter: provision of inference services, partner connector orchestration, and telemetry for service health.
- Duration: as specified in the Agreement.
- Nature and purpose: to provide inference, embedding, routing, observability, billing, and support for partner integrations.
- Categories of data subjects: end users, administrators, and technical contacts.
- Types of Personal Data: identifiers, account metadata, usage telemetry, logs (see Appendix A for sensitive categories such as payment data or special categories).

4. Lawful basis (controller responsibility)
Controller represents it has a lawful basis to provide Personal Data to Processor for the stated purposes. Processor will only process on documented instructions.

5. Subprocessors
- Authorization: Controller authorizes Processor to engage Subprocessors for performance of Services, subject to the Subprocessor obligations below.
- Subprocessor list: Processor will maintain a current list of Subprocessors and make it available via the Console or a dedicated URL.
- Prior notice: Processor will notify Controller of any new Subprocessor at least 30 days prior to onboarding. Controller may object in writing on reasonable grounds related to data protection.
- Subprocessor contract: Processor will require Subprocessors to be bound by contract terms no less protective than this Annex, including breach notification, audit rights, and data return/deletion.

6. On-premise and private deployments
- For private/on-prem deployments where Processor software is deployed inside Controller infrastructure, the Parties shall specify in Appendix B the access methods, support windows, telemetry collected, and any remote maintenance methods.
- Where Controller requires an air-gapped deployment, Processor will provide a copy of the permitted telemetry and support checklist; negotiation on-support SLAs and emergency escalation costs may apply.

7. Security measures
Processor shall implement and maintain appropriate technical and organizational measures, including but not limited to:
- Access control and least privilege; role-based access with documented approvals for elevated access.
- Encryption at rest and in transit (TLS 1.2+ for in-transit; AES-256 or equivalent for at-rest on controlled storage).
- Key management: Processor shall provide options for customer-managed keys via supported KMS/HSM integrations where supported by the deployment model.
- Logging and monitoring: collect audit logs for administrative access, configuration changes, and data access; retain logs for a minimum of 90 days unless otherwise agreed.
- Data minimization and retention: Processor will implement configurable retention controls; default telemetry retention for non-essential logs is 30 days.
- Embeddings and derived vectors: Processor recommends pseudonymization or deterministic tokenization where Controller embeds sensitive attributes; note possible re-identification risk and include mitigation options.

8. Incident and breach notification
- Definitions: "Security Incident" means any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access, loss, or disclosure of Personal Data.
- Notification timeline: Processor will notify Controller without undue delay and in any event within 72 hours of becoming aware of a Security Incident that materially affects Controller Personal Data, providing initial summary and remediation steps.
- Cooperation: Processor will provide relevant incident details, root cause analysis, corrective actions, and will assist in Controller-required notifications to supervisory authorities or data subjects as necessary.

9. Data subject requests and assistance
- Processor will, to the extent legally permitted, promptly notify Controller of any request from a data subject seeking to exercise rights under applicable law and will assist Controller in responding, at Controller’s expense for extraordinary support.

10. Transfers and localization
- Standard mechanisms: cross-border transfers will be governed by the Agreement and may rely on SCCs, adequacy decisions, or equivalent transfer tools.
- Localization requirements: if Controller requires data to remain in a specific geography, Processor shall use region-specific infrastructure where available and document the data residency approach in Appendix C.

11. Audit and compliance
- Audit rights: Controller may audit Processor once per 12-month period subject to reasonable confidentiality protections and coordination. For enterprise customers, audits may include an on-site inspection with 60 days’ notice.
- Certifications and reports: Processor will provide SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate, and penetration test summary on request where available, subject to an NDA.

12. Data return and deletion
- End of services: upon termination, Processor will, at Controller’s election, either return or securely delete Personal Data within the timeframe set out in the Agreement (default 60 days).
- Deletion verification: Processor will provide a deletion certificate or attest to deletion procedures where physical media disposal or scrubbing is required.

13. Liability and limitations
- Liability: parties agree to the liability caps and exclusions set out in the MSA, subject to carveouts for willful misconduct and gross negligence. Specific carveouts for breaches of data protection obligations may be negotiated.

14. Special provisions for partner connectors
- Connector configuration: Controller retains the right to configure which third-party services a Partner Connector may send data to; Processor will implement permissions and allowlists to enforce Controller choices.
- Connector data flow transparency: Processor will provide a per-connector audit trail showing destinations and timestamps for data forwarded to third parties for at least 180 days.
- Third-party destination compliance: Controller acknowledges responsibility to confirm destination service obligations where Controller configures connectors to send Personal Data to third-party services.

15. Negotiation options and redlines (party-friendly alternatives)
- Notice period for new subprocessor: Optional 30 days (Controller-friendly) vs 14 days (Processor-friendly).
- Incident notification: Optional 24 hours for high-severity incidents vs 72 hours baseline.
- Audit frequency: Optional once per 12 months baseline vs quarterly for high-risk engagements.

Appendices (to be populated per deal):
- Appendix A: Data inventory (fields, retention, sensitivity classification)
- Appendix B: On-prem deployment support and telemetry checklist
- Appendix C: Regional data residency commitments and controls

Internal negotiation comments (inline):
- [Internal note: consider offering a limited deletion certification (hash-based) rather than full forensic deletion report to balance legal ask vs operational cost.]
- [Internal note: include an explicit line that embeddings and derived vectors are treated as Personal Data only where they are reasonably re-identifiable; this reduces overbroad exposure but keep optional checkbox for customers who instruct otherwise.]

Action items and TODOs:
- Add link to public Subprocessor list (Console URL) prior to sending to partner.
- Legal to confirm exact SCC wording to use for EU transfers (CONFLUENCE-SEC-1245).
- Security to confirm default log retention window and options for extended retention for enterprise deals.

Draft status summary:
- Template v0.9 — internal review requested from Legal and Security. Ready for CLM intake after a round of comments.

Redlines expected from partners: subprocessor notice timing, deletion verification granularity, and breach notification SLA.

Contact for negotiations:
- Owner: Maya Chen (Legal) — maya.chen@redwood.ai
- Technical lead: Omar Alvarez (Security) — omar.alvarez@redwood.ai

End of Annex template.
